title: The Vermilion Gallery
summary: Curator Ines Marlow was found dead in the gallery vault at 7pm on opening night, beside a bronze statuette from the new collection. The doors were locked at six, and four people were still inside.

victim.name: Ines Marlow
victim.description: The gallery's curator, who had just discovered that a painting in the vault was a forgery.

suspects.name: Theo Vance
suspects.description: The artist whose work opened the season, and whose last show the curator panned.

suspects.name: Sam Okafor
suspects.description: The night guard, who holds the only keycard for the vault.

suspects.name: Lady Wren
suspects.description: A collector who sold the gallery its most expensive painting.

suspects.name: Pia Lund
suspects.description: The curator's assistant, who keeps the catalogue and the schedule.

planned_lies.says: At seven I was walking my round in the west hall. I never opened the vault.
I was waiting in the curator's office for Ines. She never came.

clues.description: Theo Vance was in the cafe at 7pm, arguing about the hanging of his canvases.
At 7pm Pia Lund saw Theo Vance and brought him a coffee.
The east hall camera shows Lady Wren in front of her painting at 7pm.
The vault door log shows the guard's keycard used at 7:04pm.
Pia Lund saw Sam Okafor carry the bronze statuette out of the packing room.
A refund demand from the curator to Lady Wren for the forged painting.

documents.title: East hall camera log
documents.body: Camera E2. 18:58 visitor enters. 19:00 to 19:12 visitor (female, grey coat, identified as Lady Wren) stands at catalogue no. 14. 19:13 visitor exits north.

documents.title: Vault door access log
documents.body: 18:02 card 19 (S. Okafor) lock. 19:04 card 19 (S. Okafor) unlock. 19:09 card 19 (S. Okafor) lock.

documents.title: Letter from the curator to Lady Wren
documents.body: Lady Wren, catalogue no. 14 is not what you sold us. The gallery requires the full price returned by Friday, or I go to the police.

documents.title: Security desk memo
documents.body: Opening night. East hall camera E2, footage 18:00 to 20:00, copied and handed to the police at their request. A second copy is held at the security desk for viewing.

documents.title: Private view invitation
documents.body: The Vermilion Gallery requests the pleasure of your company at the opening of new works by Theo Vance. Friday, from six. Doors close at six for the private view.

documents.title: Hanging plan for the season
documents.body: West hall: nos. 1 to 9, Theo Vance, new works. East hall: nos. 10 to 16, the permanent collection, including no. 14, Harbour at Dusk, acquired from Lady Wren. Vault: works awaiting authentication.

documents.title: Catering invoice
documents.body: Bellweather Catering to the Vermilion Gallery, attn. P. Lund. One hundred and twenty canapes, four cases of sparkling wine, coffee service for the cafe. Payment due in thirty days.

documents.title: Clipping from the arts pages
documents.body: Of Theo Vance's last show, the curator Ines Marlow wrote that it was competent, airless, and forgettable. Vance has said he has not forgotten it.

documents.title: Guard rota
documents.body: Friday. Day guard D. Hale, 09:00 to 18:00. Night guard S. Okafor, 18:00 to 06:00. Relief on Saturday from the agency.

documents.title: Packing room list
documents.body: Crate 3, unpacked Thursday. Bronze statuette, Vermilion collection no. 22. Marble head, no. 23. Two plinths. Both pieces to stay in the packing room until the insurer's valuation.

documents.title: Letter from the insurer
documents.body: Dear Ms. Marlow, cover on catalogue no. 14 is suspended until the authentication you requested is complete. We will need the conservator's findings in writing.

documents.title: Conservator's report on no. 14
documents.body: Canvas machine-woven, ground contains titanium white. The work cannot date from the 1890s as catalogued. My opinion is that it is a modern copy.

documents.title: Opening night run sheet
documents.body: 18:00 doors locked, private view begins. 18:30 speeches. 20:00 guests out, lights down. The artist's talk is moved to Saturday at Mr. Vance's request.

documents.title: Cafe till receipt
documents.body: Vermilion Cafe. Two espresso, one lemon cake. 18:41. Paid in cash. Thank you for visiting.

documents.title: Note from Theo Vance to the curator
documents.body: Ines, hang the triptych where people can see it or take it down. I will not be buried at the end of a corridor again. T.V.

documents.title: Electrician's work order
documents.body: West hall track lighting flickering on circuits 2 and 3. Transformer to be replaced Monday. Do not adjust the spotlights before then.

documents.title: Police call note
documents.body: Call received 19:31 from the Vermilion Gallery. A woman found dead in the vault, head wound. Four persons on the premises held for questioning.
